-OwVQHLkz3WHnuDOBHqV.content: [{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The Oratrice trembles with terrifying power, spinning its clock and balancing the scales. Furina sits at the throne of the Opera Epiclese on the left of the Oratrice, as the Traveler sits on the right, with Neuvillette in the middle as the Iudex. As the Oratrice pulses, tears start dropping from Furina's face as she realises what is about to happen in the next few moments, then I walk in. The Oratrice explodes out pulses of power and transports Furina and Neuvillette into the Realm of the Heavens. In the Opera people start screaming and it causes a chain reaction of people escaping the Opera as the floor-lights strobe azure and the chandeliers ring like struck crystal. The last echo of panic blurs into a gloss of silence, and I am left beneath the Oratrice’s yawning halo, its scales tilting toward a verdict that would devour a soul. "}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“Stop,” I say—not loud, but exact. My voice threads the engines of judgment like a needle through a storm. The machine stutters. Its clockhand skips. The air tastes of ozone and rain."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"A seam opens above the stage like a pupil widening, and starlight spills down in a thin, pale spiral. I take one step into it—and the Opera, the fleeing crowd, the velvet curtains slick with spray—fall away."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The Realm of the Heavens is not a sky, but a courtroom made from constellations. Pillars of lacquered night climb forever. Between them, rivers of script flow: laws etched in light, clauses like falling leaves. At the center, a disk of calm water bears two figures upon its mirrored face. I take one look around and realise I have been here before, but not for nearly 1000 years."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Furina kneels, small against the firmament, hands clenched in the skirts of a role she no longer owns. Her tears fall into the water and ring like chimes. Across from her, Neuvillette stands shore-still, the rain in his hair unmoving in this suspended sphere. His eyes meet mine—old, fathomless—and then shift back to Furina with a grief too careful to spill."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Above them both, the Oratrice descends as a crown and a guillotine."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“This jurisdiction is not yours,” I tell it. My words plume as mist in the cold. “Not anymore.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The scales answer with a grind that could be thunder folded into gears. Lines of casework ignite in the heavens—verdicts past, bargains struck, promises spent. It begins to weigh. What is a person, when peeled from their titles? What is a sin measured against a city’s survival? The needle twitches toward doom. "}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"I step to the water’s edge and feel the Realm test me, pricking at the borders of my will. “You claim to judge truth,” I say to the machine, “but truth is not a corpse on a table. It breathes. It changes in the telling. If you must balance, then balance all of it.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The river of script shivers. Pages of light turn. The disk widens, revealing reflections tucked beneath: a girl laughing too brightly to cover a tremor in her hands; a goddess who bargained her life to stall an old sea; the empty chair left behind, still warm."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Furina’s breath hitches. “Don’t—” She looks up, wet-lashed, throat working. “Don’t show them that.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“We aren’t ‘them’ here,” I say gently. “We’re the last listeners.” I kneel, and the water bears me. “Furina, do you want to live?”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Her eyes flick to the Oratrice, to Neuvillette, to me. “I… I don’t know how,” she whispers. The confession is a key turned in a door that expects a sword"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"\"You don't know how? How do you even know if we do Furina? Everyone doesn't, that's the meaning of life, finding your way to live while going at it\" I reply while walking around, remembering the runes that were placed there to protect Teyvat"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The Oratrice’s clock jerks. In the star-court, a new corridor of text attempts to write itself: Remedy denied. Sentence proceeds. The machine reaches for the oldest comfort—the tyranny of precedent."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"I stand and raise my hand, palm mirrored in the water. “Then hear a new precedent,” I declare, and the Realm attends."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"I speak of debts repaid in kind no ledger can total of nights Furina wore a crown of jokes because a city needed laughter more than thunder; of the way a lie told to protect can become a promise to heal; of a verdict’s true purpose—not to end a life, but to return it to the world better steered."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Words become weather here. Each clause seeds a cloud, each proof a falling star. The storm gathers above the scales. For a heartbeat, I am afraid—of failing her, of being too late, of the machine’s blind hunger. Then I feel a second palm slide into mine."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Furina’s fingers are cold, but they squeeze back."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“I submit evidence,” she says, voice thin, brave. “I submit… myself.” She looks at Neuvillette. “And I request an advocate.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“The court recognizes your request,” he replies, tone solemn as tide. He steps forward, and with him the smell of wet stone and river grass. “I will speak.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The Oratrice lowers its face to meet ours. Lights split, then braid. We three are fixed under its sight like insects pinned—except there is nothing cruel in the gaze now. It is merely vast. Waiting."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Neuvillette bows his head. “By the laws of Fontaine and the older law that water remembers every shape it has worn, I attest that Furina is not the mask she was forced to carry, but the person who bore it without breaking.” His voice softens. “I attest that mercy is the only sentence that does not lie.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The needle wavers."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"I take the last step, onto the center of the disk. The Realm tries to forbid it; the water heaves under my weight, cold claws tugging at my ankles. I answer with a simple, stubborn truth: some things are worth falling for."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“Judge,” I say to the Oratrice—not to the crown of brass and light, but to the listening presence behind it, the place where machines end and meaning begins. “If you pass this sentence, you will carve a wound into the story even you cannot close. But if you stay your hand, you do not erase the past. You make room for its future.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Silence."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Then the heavens blink and explode into a brilliant light."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The clockhand clicks backward one notch. The scales level, then settle with a hush like theater curtains folding at last. Verdict: Deferred. Remedy: Reparative. Custody: Returned."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The Realm exhales—a long, relieved breath—then breaks like glass into rain. We fall."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"I land on the Opera’s stage amid the slow applause of dripping water. The house is not empty after all; a few souls linger in the balconies, stunned witnesses to a miracle too intimate for clamor. The Oratrice hangs above us, dimmer, as if a fever has broken. Its light strokes Furina’s hair where she has tumbled to her knees, laughing, crying, brilliantly, messily alive."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Neuvillette steps down, his footfalls steady, his gaze gentled. At the lip of the stage, the first of the crowd peeks back through the doors, pulled by something older than fear: hope."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Furina looks up at me with eyes still trembling, and for the first time they are not asking for permission to pretend. “Did we win?” she asks, incredulous."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"“We didn’t lose you,” I answer."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"She scrubs at her face, smears the tears into a grin far too wide for etiquette. “Then—then I must announce it, mustn’t I? A show must have an ending.” She springs onto the proscenium, arms flung wide to the dark, returning audience. “Ladies and gentlemen of Fontaine! Tonight’s performance concludes with a surprise: an encore.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"A ripple of laughter. The chandeliers warm. Someone begins to clap in earnest, and the sound catches like fire in dry grass, spreading from box to box until it becomes a wave that breaks over the stage. Furina bows, not as an Archon, not as a liar, but as a person shamelessly, triumphantly still here. I go and hug Furina one last time and leaves Fontaine to go to Inazuma."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Neuvillette comes to stand beside her, his profile lit in river light. He does not smile; the sea seldom does. But something within him loosens, a long-held current finally choosing the open."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The Oratrice lowers its scales one last time, and this time the balance is simple: a life, set against a city’s love."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"It tips toward her for the final time."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":""}]}]

ghKcPINokSP7QeZ2kJAIwbW4v2H2.summary:
A lonely sailor named Elias finds a bottle on the shore. Inside is a letter that reads: "I've been watching you. Write back." It's signed, "The Sea." He writes a reply and tosses it into the waves. The next morning, a new letter waits on his deck: "Tell me why you're sad."
-----------
A lonely sailor named Elias finds a bottle on the shore. Inside is a letter that reads: "I've been watching you. Write back." It's signed, "The Sea." He writes a reply and tosses it into the waves. The next morning, a new letter waits on his deck: "Tell me why you're sad."
-----------

-----------
Enter your plot in as much detail as possible.

-----------
Missing the Bus on Presentation Day

Presentation day was one of the most important days of the school term. My classmates and I had been working on our projects for several weeks, and today we would finally present them to the class. I had chosen to talk about protecting the environment, and I had spent many evenings researching, designing colorful slides, and practicing my speech in front of my family. Although I felt nervous, I was also excited because I knew I had prepared well.

The night before, I checked my school bag carefully. I packed my laptop, notebook, presentation notes, and a bottle of water. I even ironed my school uniform so that everything would be ready for the next morning. Before going to bed, I set two alarms to make sure I would not oversleep.

Unfortunately, things did not go as planned. During the night, my phone battery ran out, so neither of my alarms went off. I woke up much later than usual when sunlight shone through my window. As soon as I looked at the clock, my heart began to race. I jumped out of bed, quickly brushed my teeth, changed into my uniform, grabbed my school bag, and rushed out of the house without eating breakfast.

I ran as fast as I could towards the bus stop. My shoes slapped against the pavement while I hoped the bus would still be there. As I reached the corner of the street, I saw the school bus pulling away. I waved my hands and shouted for the driver to stop, but the bus continued down the road. I stood there breathing heavily, watching it disappear. I could not believe I had missed the bus on the most important day of the term.

I immediately called my father and explained what had happened. Luckily, he was working from home that morning and agreed to drive me to school. Although he left as soon as possible, the roads were crowded with morning traffic. Every red traffic light felt like forever. I kept looking at the clock, imagining my classmates sitting in the classroom while the teacher called my name. The closer we got to school, the more anxious I became.

When we finally arrived, I thanked my father and hurried to my classroom. I stopped outside the door to catch my breath before knocking gently. My teacher opened the door, and every student turned to look at me. My face became hot with embarrassment. I quietly apologized for being late and explained that I had missed the school bus despite my efforts to get there on time.

My teacher listened patiently and understood that it had been an accident. She smiled kindly and told me to take my seat. She said I could give my presentation after the next student. Her understanding made me feel much calmer, and I was grateful for the second chance.

As I waited for my turn, I reviewed my notes one last time. My hands were shaking slightly, but I reminded myself that I had practiced many times. When my name was called, I walked to the front of the classroom, took a deep breath, and began my presentation.

At first, my voice was a little shaky, but after a few minutes I became more confident. I explained the importance of protecting the environment by reducing waste, recycling, planting trees, and saving energy. I used pictures and examples to make my presentation interesting. My classmates listened carefully, and some even nodded as I spoke. When I finished, they applauded warmly.

Thanks to that experience, I have become more responsible, organized, and confident whenever I face important challenges.

hsaBuah3qBSdtt1bf2yt4ne9IxD3.summary:
-----------
hello
-----------
I’ve always had a super thick skin. In our friend group, we roast each other constantly, and I’m always the first to laugh when someone makes fun of my terrible haircut or my trash grades. I just assumed everyone was wired the same way. To me, a joke was just a joke—low stakes, zero malice. But I learned the hard way that my "strength" isn't a universal standard, and it happened at the expense of a classmate named Zuko.

It happened during our group project presentations in history class. Zuko was up, and you could tell he was visibly terrified. He’s a quiet guy who mostly keeps to himself, and public speaking clearly wasn't his thing. As he stood by the projector, his voice kept cracking, and he accidentally tripped over the laptop cord, sending his notes flying everywhere.

The room went dead silent. From the back row, I thought it was the perfect chaotic moment for a meme. I snapped a quick, blurry photo of him scrambling for his papers and threw it onto my private Snapchat story with the caption: “Me trying to hold my life together before finals week 😂💀.”

In my head, it wasn't malicious. I wasn’t trying to bully him; I thought it was a relatable joke about school stress using a funny, chaotic image. If someone did that to me, I would’ve re-shared it and laughed.

The bell rang twenty minutes later, and as everyone was packing up, I saw Zuko sitting at his desk, staring intently at his phone. The color had completely drained from his face. He didn’t look angry; he just looked entirely defeated. One of his friends whispered something to him, pointing in my direction, and Zuko quickly shoved his phone into his backpack, kept his head down, and practically bolted out of the classroom.

A mutual friend of ours stopped by my desk. “Dude, you need to take that down. Zuko has massive anxiety about public speaking, and he was freaking out about this presentation all week.”

My stomach instantly dropped. I deleted the story right then and there, but the damage was already done.

I spent the next period feeling sick. The whole "I didn't mean anything by it" excuse kept running through my mind, but looking at how Zuko had reacted, that excuse felt completely empty. I realized that just because I can shrug off a roast doesn't mean everyone else is carrying the same weight. Zuko wasn't "weak"—he was just fighting a battle with anxiety that I knew absolutely nothing about, and I had weaponized his worst moment for a couple of cheap digital laughs.

At the end of the day, I caught up to him by his locker. My heart was pounding, which was rare for me.

“Hey, Zuko,” I said, rubbing the back of my neck. He stiffened up, avoiding my eyes. “Look, I wanted to apologize for the Snap story. It was a stupid, thoughtless thing to post. I thought I was just being funny, but it was mean, and I’m really sorry.”

Zuko was quiet for a second, then let out a heavy sigh. “I just hate that everyone’s laughing at me now,” he said softly.

“They aren't, man. I took it down immediately,” I told him. “It’s on me, completely. I was a jerk.”

He gave a small, weary nod. It wasn't an instant fix, and things were awkward for a while. But walking away, the way I viewed the world totally changed. I learned that impact matters way more than intent, and true strength isn’t about having thick skin—it’s about knowing when a joke stops being funny and starts being cruel.

l1uTxUvFpQVfYGEi6dDE8kFs8EI2.summary:
The number glowed faintly under the moonlight—an old, faded jersey stretched across a broad silhouette. James barely made out the white numerals before his heart dropped into his stomach.

Eleven.

That number had haunted him for years. The same number his bully had worn during every practice, every game, every hallway shove. He could still hear the laughter, the taunts, the name-calling that followed him home each day. And now—after all these years—that jersey was closing in on him.

He grabbed his friend's wrist and ducked behind a rusted dumpster. "Don't move. Don't breathe."

The footsteps grew louder. Closer. A shadow passed the alley entrance, stopped, and turned slowly. James pressed himself against the cold brick, his friend's hand gripping his in the dark.

Ten seconds. Twenty. Then the footsteps continued, fading into the distance.

They stayed still for two more minutes before James finally exhaled.

"I thought I left this town behind for good," he whispered.

His friend looked at him—eyes searching, not quite understanding. "Who was that?"

James couldn't answer. Not yet. Instead, he nodded toward the old path that led up the hill. "We need to keep moving. The hangout isn't far."

They ran in silence, weaving through back alleys and overgrown shortcuts that James remembered from childhood. His lungs burned. The night air was cold against his sweat-soaked skin. Every shadow seemed alive, every creak a signal that he'd been found.

Finally, they reached the clearing. The old treehouse. The meeting spot. The one place that had ever felt safe.

James stopped.

The treehouse was gone. Boarded up. Demolished. Nothing remained but a concrete slab and a pile of splintered wood, as if someone had erased his last good memory.

He stood there, staring at the rubble, the air leaving his lungs differently now.

"It's gone..."

His friend stepped beside him, quiet for a long moment. Then, without a word, he placed a hand on James's shoulder—steady, firm, present.

"I'm sorry, man."

James couldn't speak. But he didn't need to. For the first time all night, he wasn't running. He wasn't hiding. He was just standing there, in the ruins of a place that no longer existed, with someone who hadn't left.

And somehow, that mattered more than reaching the hangout ever could.

-OwVsWXV-7vSu8cUicbD.content: [{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"It was 9:00PM and it was getting late. It was presentation day the next day but I was fully focused on my video games all night and completely ignored the fact that it was almost midnight. My brother walked in and told said, \"Adam, If I were you, I'd get to bed right now. You do not want to wake up late and miss the bus, especially on presentation day\". I ignored him as I was confident I am able to wake up on time the next morning. This was a grieve mistake I made which I wish that I could take back even until this day."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":" I woke up the next morning with a familiar voice screaming my name at the top of their lungs, \"ADAM WAKE UP YOUR GONNA MISS THE BUS!!!\". It was my mother. The first thing I saw when I opened my eyes was my clock saying \"7:50AM\". School was about to begin in 10 minutes and I am tucked in my sheets sleeping like a baby. The shock made me instantly jolt out of bed and I rushed towards the bathroom and took the quickest and uncleanliest shower of life. I scrambled trying to find my uniform until my bad day got even more worse. I realized My uniform were still dripping wet in the washing machine. At that moment I felt like disappearing completely from the guilt and regret I felt at that moment, it was killing me. I wore a grey sweatpants and the closest shirt I could find which was a oversized hoodie, completely violating the school dress code. At that point nothing worried me more than reaching school and at least salvage myself with my presentation. My mom had made me breakfast but I completely ignored her and put on my shoes and grabbed my dream home model with me and rushed out of my house towards the bus. That was until the worst day of my life somehow became even more worse. I could see the bus driving off in the distance. I started sprinting as fast as I can towards the bus and the last thing I remembered that I'm not wearing my school shoes until I ultimately tripped on my shoe lace and fell down on the rough asphalt together with my model, completely destroying it and my knees. All I felt at that moment was regret, so much so I didn't realize I bruised mt knee from the impact. My brothers voice kept echoing in my head of him reminding me to go to sleep early. It was torturing me. A grey sedan pulled up next to me moments later. The rims of the tire looked familiar until I got myself up to my feet and saw my brother offering to drive me to school, that was until he saw my destroyed model and the tears dropping down my face. He drove me back home and my mom had to go out of her was towards the school to give an excuse on why I was absent but she still never told me what she said until today. I didn't have the courage to get out of the car when my brother pulled over in the driveway. I was weeping in my bed for the rest of the day. Tears of regret, guilt and embarrassment. I missed out on an opportunity to present on something I have been working hard for, I badly injured my knee, I left the breakfast my mom made with love to become cold and I had to trouble both my brother and my mother all because I refused to sacrifice a few hours of video games for sleep. This one moment of life has forever became a reminder for me to not be so stubborn because the smallest of actions can lead to the biggest of impacts, even in a negative way."}]}]

I went to school but my school blow up
-----------
It was a Tuesday. Everyone went to work and school like a robot, doing the same task repeatedly. I was waiting for my school bus and scrolling on my phone, watching some funny videos. My mom told me not to scroll phone as I will miss my bus, but I still will do because I wanted to kill the boredom of waiting the bas that will arrive in a century. “BiBi” The bus had arrived. I walked to the bus and sat in a corner.
The bus had arrived at the school, and I stepped down on the stairs. I went to the old hallway and passed through principal room and library. Finally, I reached my classroom. I put my bag on the chair and prepared my presentation for History class. Everyone was ready but except me who is a turtle, still editing the slide that I missed out. The bell rang and teacher came into the classroom and was excited to see our presentation.
Everyone was slowly waiting for their turn to present their own masterpiece. I know that mine is bad as I prepared at the very last minute and my classmates know that I am a procrastinating person. Out of sudden, I saw one of my classmate was having messy hair like they just woke up from bed. I quickly screenshot and put in my presentation. After waiting for long time, is my turn to present my own “masterpiece”. I gave my teacher and classmates a speech and as soon as I was about to end, I showed them the picture I just added. Everyone was laughing. But not the classmate that was in the picture. He stood up and scolded me very loudly, even louder than the whale. He smashed the door and went outside of the class. I was stunned. I quickly rushed to him and comforted him, but he doesn’t even care about it.
After school, I went to find him. He was better than at History class which is good for me to comfort him. As a result, he still didn’t even want to forgive me. I wanted to beg him to forget and forgive me but is harder than my math exam. Back to home, I immediately wrote a letter about apologies to him of what I did today. I also promised I will not do it again. I wrote all my regrets in the letter.
Wednesday, everyone did the same as yesterday. I waited for the bus but putting down my phone and thinking how to be good with him. I don’t really understand about him as I am not close to him, we are just classmates. I gave him the letter in school and he finally accepted it. I felt so relieved and thank you him that he finally forgave me. I promised this would not happen to everyone again and I am good friend with him.

-OwVQR5kYBBEUrU4LXcR.content: [{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Footsteps thudding faster than my heartbeat, luggage wheels rumbling across the metal flooring. People were rushing in and out of the gates, some with phone at their ears whilst others with babies in their arms. I skimmed briefly, the tall pillars of white concrete holding up glass window panels, rows and rows of \"stainless\" steel chairs rusting at every corner. I looked up and I saw airplanes flying across at every second, so close to the roof, it feels like it could fall and crash at any mintute. The never ending metal trail abruptly blended into a dark black carpet with grey seams, I followed, thinking magically it would take me somewhere I needed to be. My legs paced forward, each step I took, my head spun a 360 to make sure I was going to the right place, even though I had no clue where the right place was. My fist grabbed onto my luggage handle tighter, there was so many stations and so many walkways leading to even more stations. I squinted my eyes trying to make do of the directory in full mandarin, acting like I could understand with my half bucket level of mandarin, as what they would call it \"ban tong sui\". "}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":""}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"I turned back, I looked at the airplane entrance, then I look back at the vast endless horizon of a airport nightmare. The one narrow entrance felt a lot more safer, so my body inched closer to it, its not too late to turn back right, turn back home, home to a place where I can mix my mandarin with the Bahasa Melayu language and my excellent English skills, ah yes that a I can do. Home to a place where everything feels more certain, a place where I can at least navigate. Yet again the scents of chromium plated architecture, the coffee & garlic aroma sipping from the cafes and bakeries, the fresh perfume of flowers wrapped into \"welcome home\" bouquets, I knew I had to stay. I strived down again, more confident than ever, passing the giant posters of my favourite cdrama actors and actress, pass the countless stores of panda and bamboo themed souvenirs, down to a metal arch, I took my phone out and opened google translate, (I still had express VPN on, thank god for that) I scanned the giant signage. Loading..loading and loading...finally! The words \"Arrival Terminal\" plastered across my phone screen, I grabbed onto my giant luggage, so tall it reached up to my ribcage, I was contemplating life, \"Why did I even pack so many things\" replayed in my brain again and again. I strapped my extra bag onto the handle to get a little space for my hands to move. I just kept going, through the horizontal escalator, following the turns and curves until somehow I stumbled into another signage, I scan, I read \"Security Check\" ah yes, I found my nest destination. I guess, I can figure my way...I guess I can take on the world."}]}]

-OwQnBYbr6-Of--uhOjX.content: [{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"It's a typical Tuesday, a day not any different from any other day. I live alone in this house for as long as I remember. It was 7AM in the morning and the air was cold. I was greeted by a cool breeze as I opened the windows of my living room. As I turn my back facing the window, I met eyes with an old woman who was sitting on my couch. Strangely enough, she did not knock on my front door, but how did she manage to get in? She was wearing a vibrant blue dress and a silver ring on her finger which appeared oddly familiar. I was physically unable to take my eyes of her finger until it hit me, it was my late grandmother's ring. Time pasts as she stares blanky into my soul, then she points at my phone as I reach for it."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":""}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Over the next few hours, the old woman showed and warned me about impossible things, me in a hospital gown I have never worn, a rainy road you've never driven, a mirror in a house you never entered. Each vision left me a physical mark- a bruise, a scar and a smell of wet earth. Secretly, I researched my grandmother's life and discovered she died in a car crash on a rainy night thirty years ago. She was rushing to apologize to someone while I was in her car as a baby. The mirror that the old woman warned me about is in the house she was driving to that night. The crash was intentional, she swerved to avoid hitting a deer, but maybe she didn't have to."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":""}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"The old woman points at a calendar date: three days from now. That's the anniversary of the car crash. I knew something was up, as if the future had sent someone to me. Quickly, without a second thought, I drive to the old house. It appeared abandoned and vines have grown all over the concrete of the house. As I made my way into the house, the first thing I saw was the mirror. It was cracked. I reached forward to feel the crack of the mirror, I saw the full memory: my grandmother saw something in that mirror the night of the crash, a future version of me, standing exactly where I am now, looking broken. She swerved not for the deer, but because the vision terrified her. She wasn't trying to save herself. She was trying to save me from ever seeing what she saw. The old woman finally smiles, points at me, and fades. I realize the warning wasn't about trusting the mirror, it was about trusting that her love was worth the crash."}]}]

He rushed over to analyse what his dinner was about to be. He could not make out exactly what it was, but, considering the fact that he was famished, he decided anything as edible looking as this should suffice. He grabbed the snack in his mouth and chewed. As he swallowed the snack, the flavour he was met with was something in between rich honey and rare, tender meat. It was unlike anything he had ever tasted, but the flavour truly changed him. As he attempted to walk around the landfill and scavenge for more, nothing really felt the same. The rough voices of the workers at the landfill seemed to turn from gibberish to something he could comprehend. He didn't understand what was happening, but the sudden change struck fear in his heart, and he began to regret taking the strange snack. "}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"\"Where is that darn fox?\" said one of the voices."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"\"I hate working here,\" said another."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Hao Hern realised something. He could understand them now! All the nonsense he was hearing became completely understandable with the consumption of that one strange snack. "}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"With his newfound ability, Hao Hern immediately stopped searching for more food, and decided to find something he had been searching for his whole life; his parents. "}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"They were captured by humans long ago, and he wanted to reunite with them. -OwWUluvvVeDMmE7iQPo.content: [{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"Last Saturday, our school went to a museum for field trip. This field trip is very fun, but it gave me a really nervous experience that I have never been."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"On 10 o'clock we arrived at the museum. There were a lot of people outside the museum and waiting. The teacher guides us went in the museum. I was following my own group to watch around the museum.The museum was a dull hum of whispers and footsteps. The air in museum is cool and still. Sunlight slanted through the tall windows, catching dust that floated like slow snow. Our teacher's voice droned at the front, but my eyes wandered. And at this moment, I thought I was following the group, but I wasn't paying attention to the path and teacher. I was too busy staring at the glass case.I stopped in front of a small, dark painting. It wasn't loud or flashy, but something about it held me still. When I finally looked up, the hallway was empty."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"My heart dropped. I start to be nervous. I tried to find my group and teachers. I went left there is no one. I went right there were also none of my classmates or teachers. Just silent exhibits staring back. I started walking fast, then jogging, my footsteps echoing in the quiet. Every hallway looked the same. - My hands felt cold and clammy. I kept swallowing, but my throat stayed dry. My footsteps sounded too loud in the silence, like they were announcing that I didn't belong here. Every corner led to another painting I didn't recognize. I was completely lost. The empty hallway stretched in both directions, and not a single voice broke the quiet. I stood still, waiting for someone to call my name, but no one did. I wrapped my arms around myself. Every shadow in the corner made me freeze. My breath got shorter, and the walls suddenly felt too close. I wrapped my arms around myself and started walking faster, hoping to find someone, anyone. But every turn looked the same. Rows of old paintings stared down at me like strangers judging my every step. My footsteps echoed too loud. I felt small. I felt invisible. I stopped and looked around, but the world kept spinning. I didn't know which way was forward or back. All I wanted was to hear my teacher's voice just one familiar sound in this quiet, lonely place. I was jogging in the museum and suddenly went into another part in museum. There were a lot of people around me. They are chatting watching or do something else, but I still feel lonely and fear. They are all moving only me was standing in the middle of the way. Suddenly, i heard someone was calling me but when i turned my head they were all strangers."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":"When I spotted my classmate's jacket up ahead, I almost cried. I hurried over and quietly slipped back into the group. Nobody knew I had been lost. But I knew. And I would never forget that feeling.This must be the most unforgettable field trip in my life."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"text":""}]}]
